hints: Resolve all forces horizontally and vertically. Set each sum to zero since the system is in equilibrium.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium, taking the direction of the horizontal component of $F$ (to the left) as positive:
$$F\cos\alpha + 50\cos 45^\circ = 40\cos 60^\circ + 20\cos 30^\circ$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 40\cos 60^\circ + 20\cos 30^\circ - 50\cos 45^\circ$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 40(0.5) + 20(0.866025) - 50(0.707107)$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 20 + 17.3205 - 35.3553 = 1.9652\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium, taking upwards as positive:
$$F\sin\alpha + 40\sin 60^\circ = 20\sin 30^\circ + 50\sin 45^\circ$$
$$F\sin\alpha = 50\sin 45^\circ + 20\sin 30^\circ - 40\sin 60^\circ$$
$$F\sin\alpha = 50(0.707107) + 20(0.5) - 40(0.866025)$$
$$F\sin\alpha = 35.3553 + 10 - 34.6410 = 10.7143\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Set up standard Cartesian coordinates where the positive $x$-axis points to the right and the positive $y$-axis points upwards.

State the equilibrium conditions for a coplanar force system:
$$\sum F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum F_y = 0$$

Resolve all four forces horizontally:
The $40\text{ N}$ force acts at $60^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis: $+40\cos 60^\circ$.
The $20\text{ N}$ force acts at $30^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis: $+20\cos 30^\circ$.
The $50\text{ N}$ force acts at $45^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis: $-50\cos 45^\circ$.
The force $F$ acts at angle $\alpha$ above the negative $x$-axis: $-F\cos\alpha$.
Set the algebraic sum to zero:
$$-F\cos\alpha + 40\cos 60^\circ + 20\cos 30^\circ - 50\cos 45^\circ = 0$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 40\cos 60^\circ + 20\cos 30^\circ - 50\cos 45^\circ$$
Substitute numerical values:
$$F\cos\alpha = 40(0.5) + 20(0.866025) - 50(0.707107)$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 20 + 17.3205 - 35.3553 = 1.9652\text{ N}$$

Resolve all four forces vertically:
The $40\text{ N}$ force acts upwards: $+40\sin 60^\circ$.
The $20\text{ N}$ force acts downwards: $-20\sin 30^\circ$.
The $50\text{ N}$ force acts downwards: $-50\sin 45^\circ$.
The force $F$ acts upwards: $+F\sin\alpha$.
Set the algebraic sum to zero:
$$F\sin\alpha + 40\sin 60^\circ - 20\sin 30^\circ - 50\sin 45^\circ = 0$$
$$F\sin\alpha = 50\sin 45^\circ + 20\sin 30^\circ - 40\sin 60^\circ$$
Substitute numerical values:
$$F\sin\alpha = 50(0.707107) + 20(0.5) - 40(0.866025)$$
$$F\sin\alpha = 35.3553 + 10 - 34.6410 = 10.7143\text{ N}$$

Compute the magnitude $F$ by combining the orthogonal components with Pythagoras theorem:
$$F = \sqrt{(F\cos\alpha)^2 + (F\sin\alpha)^2}$$
$$F = \sqrt{(1.9652)^2 + (10.7143)^2} = \sqrt{3.8620 + 114.7962} = \sqrt{118.6582} \approx 10.9\text{ N}$$

Compute the angle $\alpha$ using the tangent ratio:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{F\sin\alpha}{F\cos\alpha} = \frac{10.7143}{1.9652} \approx 5.4520$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}(5.4520) \approx 79.6^\circ$$
